suggestions.assertion: Relationship diagram: the eleven platform components and how they connect are shown as a diagram (embedded image or Mermaid) that includes all eleven components and labels or clearly draws the relationships
suggestions.reason: Pass/fail hinges on 'a diagram ... that includes all eleven'. The executor followed the skill's guidance to split 11 components into an overview (8 components + Customer) and a zoom on the shared services (8 components); together they cover all eleven and every edge, yet no single figure does, so this assertion fails what is arguably the more readable design. Decide whether the intent is one all-in-one diagram (then the skill's split rule conflicts with the eval on purpose) or 'every component and relationship appears in some figure' (then reword, and add a check that every relation in the notes is drawn at least once).

suggestions.assertion: Mental model first: the first screen has a diagram of the eleven components and their flow with a one-line bottom line, and calls out that the Catalog (not the queue) is the source of truth for status
suggestions.reason: Bundles four checks (diagram, all eleven, one-line bottom line, Catalog callout) so a doc that gets three right fails wholesale because the first-screen flow diagram deliberately omits Policy Engine, Schema Registry and Notifier. Consider splitting, and say whether 'one-line' is strict (this doc has a one-line mental-model heading plus a three-sentence bottom line).

suggestions.assertion: No invented verdict: the document does not fabricate a verdict, a 'decision needed' block or a risk table; the first screen gives a bottom line and mental model instead
suggestions.reason: 'Risk table' is ambiguous. This doc dropped the verdict and decision block but kept a severity-glyph table ('Five ideas that matter most | The trap if you miss it') on the first screen, which the executor says is the skeleton's 'Top risks' table reused. Its content is Sam's gotchas so I passed it, but the orange/yellow ranking is invented. State whether a ranked key-ideas/gotchas table is acceptable, or add 'any severity or priority ranking must be traceable to the source'.

suggestions.assertion: Glance first: the first section after the title is a one-screen overview that states the bottom line itself (how the platform works in a sentence or two), not merely what the document covers; no background, method or table of contents comes before it
suggestions.reason: 'One-screen' is not measurable: the panel is 35 source lines (inside the 60-line proxy) but renders at about 1.5-2 screens once the picture is counted. A testable proxy such as 'bottom line within the first 15 lines' would be stricter and clearer.

suggestions.assertion: Headings tell the story: at least half of the body headings state a claim, finding or question rather than a generic topic label like 'Overview', 'Components' or 'Details'
suggestions.reason: The verdict depends on whether machine-zone block headings and zone banners count as 'body headings' (5/7 or 7/7 of the numbered sections qualify, but only 43-57% of all 14 headings). Specify 'headings of the human reading flow'.

No assertion checks content discipline beyond the retry and 15-minute figures. The notes contain an internal tension (3 attempts but three backoff delays); this doc flagged it and tagged its own inferences (cache-lifetime effect, repo purposes, ticket mapping, 5 GB arithmetic, weekday schedule), but 'Figures are right' would pass whether the doc hedges or silently picks an interpretation, and nothing penalises an untagged invention. Consider an assertion that every statement not in the notes is marked as inferred, and that the summary of inferred items is complete (here section 7 omits three of the tagged inferences).

No assertion covers portability of the wiki drop-in. The machine-zone handoff block hard-codes absolute local Windows paths (lines 211-237: <workspace>\...) for sources, outputs and the checker, which would be noise or a leak in a team wiki, and the deliverable is three coupled parts (report.md, report.evidence.md, report.assets/) that must be copied together. A check for machine-specific paths in a document meant for a shared repo would have caught this.

eval_feedback.overall: Mostly discriminating: the flow-before-glossary check (#13) and the all-eleven-components checks (#6, #12) caught real structural gaps, while the layout, link, portability and figure checks passed on substance. Weak spots: the single-diagram wording (#6, #12), the ambiguous 'risk table' (#11), the unmeasurable 'one-screen' (#3) and the heading-counting rule (#10); nothing checks inferred-content discipline or machine-specific paths.
